definition: GPT-5.4 (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5.4) is a large language model (LLM) released by OpenAI on March 5, 2026.
details: OpenAI initially released the model in two variants, GPT-5.4 Thinking and GPT-5.4 Pro. Neither is available to free-tier users. On March 17, OpenAI released GPT-5.4 mini and GPT-5.4 nano. GPT-5.4 mini is available to free-tier users, and GPT-5.4 nano is only available via the OpenAI API. Through the OpenAI API, GPT-5.4 mini and GPT-5.4 nano are four times more expensive than their GPT-5 equivalents. In technical benchmarks, OpenAI reported a 33% reduction in factual errors compared to GPT-5.2. Performance improvements were focused on professional workflows. GPT-5.4 has built-in computer use capabilities, and improved deep research capabilities. In the benchmark OSWorld-Verified, which scores large language models' ability to use desktop environments, GPT-5.4 scored 75%, compared to GPT-5.2's 47.3% and the average person's 72.4%.

explainer.lead: GPT-5.4 is OpenAI’s large language model for professional work, research, and operating desktop software. Its release includes several variants with different access levels, and OpenAI reports substantially fewer factual errors than in GPT-5.2.

tiers.eli5: It's a smarter version of a chatbot that makes fewer factual mistakes, with small, cheaper versions sold separately.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick Thinking or Pro for hard tasks and mini or nano for cost-sensitive API work; mini is open to free-tier users, nano is API-only. A pitfall: through the API, mini and nano cost four times more than their GPT-5 equivalents.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a series of GPT large language models, with Thinking and Pro released first and mini and nano added March 17; OpenAI reports the 33% error reduction but publishes no full benchmark table in the given facts.

flow: A user supplies a professional, research, or desktop task to an available GPT-5.4 variant.
The model processes the request and produces language or actions for the task.
When appropriate, built-in computer use operates a desktop environment, while deep research supports research work.
The resulting answer or completed computer actions are returned to the user.
explainer.origin: OpenAI released GPT-5.4 on March 5, 2026, initially offering Thinking and Pro variants. It added mini and nano on March 17.
explainer.lineage: GPT-5.4 follows GPT-5.2, against which OpenAI reports a 33% reduction in factual errors. Its mini and nano variants also have GPT-5 equivalents, which cost one-quarter as much through the API.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPT-5.4 combines language generation with desktop computer use and research capabilities, extending the kinds of tasks a model can handle. Its OSWorld-Verified score of 75% exceeded both GPT-5.2’s 47.3% and the reported human average of 72.4%.

explainer.example: A developer routes bulk classification to GPT-5.4 nano via the API and reserves GPT-5.4 Pro for hard reasoning, paying four times the GPT-5 rate for the nano calls.
